rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a material template. Both memoranda reject private bills compensating contractors for losses on fixed-price Government contracts, conclude that the contractual record creates no Government liability or equitable basis for relief, warn against Government underwriting of contractor losses, and reject preferential treatment relative to other contractors. The child adapts this same argumentative sequence to a different construction contract and adds a competitive-bidding rationale. C11 has a notably similar risk-and-profit policy argument, while C06 shares the rejection of Government responsibility for private commercial losses, but neither matches the child's structure and factual setting as closely as C03.

shared_material.child_excerpt: there is no basis for affording relief to the contractor on equitable grounds
shared_material.parent_excerpt: my examination of the record in this case does not lead me to believe that there is an equitable basis for this claim
shared_material.explanation: Both turn from legal or contractual analysis to an express rejection of equitable relief.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Relieving bidders of losses ... would ... deprive the government of benefits resulting from favorable circumstances ... while requiring compensation for losses encountered as a result of unfavorable circumstances.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: My approval of this bill would establish the undesirable principle of Government underwriting any wartime losses incurred by contractors providing goods and services to the Government
shared_material.explanation: Both invoke the same policy against shifting a contractor's performance losses to the Government after a fixed-price bargain.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There are no circumstances in this case that would serve to distinguish it from others wherein contractors with the United States have suffered losses
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am unable to perceive any circumstances which would warrant preferential treatment for the claimant to the detriment of other wartime contractors.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive parallel conclusion: no circumstances justify singling out the claimant from similarly situated Government contractors.
